note: Dickinson Parks & Recreation area on Patterson Lake (Dickinson Reservoir), with a swimming beach, boat dock and the Crooked Crane Trail. The modern sites stand in one row among planted tree rows between a railway line and the beach area; the primitive sites are in a separate area east of the beach. --Claude
summary: Park district page + 2024 brochure map: 22 modern 30/50-amp + water $30 (entrance included), 15 primitive $20; max 40 ft, #22 pull-through; showers, dump; reserve-only on WebTrac; season May 8-Oct 13 2026 (closed now, reopens May 2027); honors Good Sam / Passport America / America the Beautiful, seniors 50% off. Lakeview stands for the west-end modern sites (~80 m over open grass); pin ok.
flags: WATERFRONT: stored lakeview stands, narrowly. The modern sites are one row along the park road (west end cul-de-sac with M21/M22 at about 46.8664,-102.8549; shore at about 46.8658,-102.8551); from that end the nearest shore of the lake's NE arm is ~75-85 m SSW over open mown grass with a few bare trees. The eastern modern sites (M1-M12) are 150-200 m from the water behind the spruce row, bathhouse, picnic shelter and playground: no view. Primitive sites P1-P15 (about 46.8670,-102.8495) are ~100 m from the beach shore behind a tree row and the beach parking lot. No site is near enough for lakefront. If AWH reads 80 m as too far for a view, not waterfront is the alternative.

WILDLIFE AREA: no wildlife-agency camping rule applies to the campground: Dickinson Parks runs it ('owned and managed by Dickinson Parks & Recreation District'); the Crooked Crane Trail's primitive section 'runs through the Wildlife Management Area along the south side' and hunting is allowed only west of 115th/114th Ave SW, walking access. Camping is 'allowed in designated areas only and must be reserved in advance'. No closed nights other than the season.

DISCOUNTS: written from the page's own words ('we do honor senior passes such as America the Beautiful, Passport America and Good Sam'); it does not state the discount amounts, and the sentence sits in the entrance-fee paragraph, so AWH may prefer to keep only the senior 50%.

BASE: $30 modern kept as base. Primitive sites ($20, 'parking space only', 3 nights in 30) are drawn with tent icons on the brochure map and the page gives no length, so whether a 23-ft rig fits is unstated.
RAILWAY: the brochure map draws a railroad along the north edge of the modern camping row (imagery: a main line ~90 m north of the sites); kept in the note as setting.
ALGAE: 'UPDATE 8-28-26: We are currently in an Advisory for Blue Green Algae' - seasonal water-quality notice, not a campground closure.

PIN: stored 46.86656,-102.85315 sits in the tree rows just north of the modern sites' road (~40 m): ok. Phone 701-456-2056 matches ('Campground: 701.456.2056 (in-season)'; admin office 701-456-2074 off-season). Website correct.
